content:
This week, Apple continues to steadily expand its Apple Sports app, offering tennis fans a new way to follow some of the most important events in addition to broadening its football coverage. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds new football leagues and tennis schedule

When Apple first launched the Apple Sports app, the experience was quite limited in terms of both availability and the actual sports covered.

Since then, the app has grown on both fronts, expanding to over 170 countries and regions while continuing to add support for new sports, leagues, and events.

For example, earlier this year, Apple Sports launched in 90 new countries and rolled out a range of features built around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports has rolled out another single update, adding Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League, and the South African Premier Division to its football lineup.

In addition, the app can now let tennis fans "follow draws live [...], including the brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," Apple said, adding that users can "see the full lineup and results for every round at a glance."

Here are the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

The football lineup continues to grow with the addition of Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League, and the South African Premier Division. Tennis fans can now follow live draws in Apple Sports, including the brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events. See the matchups and results for every round at a glance.

Are you using Apple Sports? Let us know in the comments.
